title: Unchecked Thread Departure (ID Reuse Race)
pattern: Iterating over a list of active threads or using thread IDs to index global tables without holding a lock that prevents threads from exiting and having their IDs recycled.
why_bad: Thread IDs are recycled rapidly by the OS. Accessing a thread pointer or ID outside of a synchronization block that guarantees its existence leads to logging status for the wrong thread, or memory corruption.
detection: Iterating over active thread data structures without acquiring an exit-coordinating lock (such as `departing_thread_lock`).
counterexample: Acquiring a global registration lock during traversal that blocks threads from completing their exit sequence.
